questions.q: What is the main point of the author's story?
options: Ski resorts should close terrain after storms, as the loss of his friends proved
Close friendships among teenagers can turn into rivalries when stakes become high
A risk's severe downside is easy to overlook, as an avalanche took his friends
Ski racing teaches discipline, which investors can use to avoid costly mistakes
questions.explain: He tells of two friends lost in an out-of-bounds avalanche after a small slide had seemed harmless.

questions.q: What kind of snow conditions created the avalanche danger in February 2001?
options: Fresh light powder sitting on a hard icy crust
Heavy wet snow on top of light fluffy snow
Thick wet slush sitting over a frozen granular base
A thin crust of ice over deep packed powder
questions.explain: Three feet of heavy, wet snow fell on top of earlier light, fluffy snow.

questions.q: How did the narrator plan to avoid hitchhiking the second time?
options: Take a chairlift down
He would pick them up in his truck
Have Ahren drive them
They would ski to Alpine Meadows
questions.explain: He offered to pick Brendan and Bryan up in his truck on the back-country road.

questions.q: What did the narrator point to as proof that his friends weren't at a party?
options: Their lift tickets had been scanned at the base of the Alpine Meadows chair
Their car keys were still in the lodge, so they had not driven anywhere
Their lockers were empty, so their gear had been loaded into Bryan's truck
Their sneakers were in the locker room, so their ski boots were on their feet
questions.explain: He pointed to their sneakers on the locker room floor at 9 pm.

questions.q: What does the author imply about the first small avalanche that morning?
options: It was a warning sign that went unheeded
It was set off by ski patrol
It only happened to him by chance and not to the others
It proved the slope was safe
questions.explain: He mentioned it to rescuers and they instantly understood the danger; the group had shrugged it off as awesome.
